nonblocking_risks.title: No clean Linux/Python 3.11 CI execution of H1 is in the package
nonblocking_risks.detail: The defect was observed in GitHub Actions (ubuntu, setup-python 3.11, `pip install pre-commit` then `pre-commit install --install-hooks`). All reproduction and parent validation ran on macOS with Python 3.12.13. The implementer explicitly recorded 'Linux/Python 3.11 CI NOT_RUN'. The repair mechanism (pre-commit-managed venv + pip-installed jsonschema) is platform-generic and the same pattern is already used by the proof-embedded-audit-schema hook in the same config, so the risk is low, but the ultimate CI outcome for H1 is not evidenced here.

nonblocking_risks.title: Isolated reproduction installed from an offline wheelhouse repacked from local caches, not from a package index
nonblocking_risks.detail: `pip install pre-commit` against the index failed ('from versions: none'). The implementer built a wheelhouse by extracting cached pip `.body` wheels and repacking uv-cache distributions with RECORD hash/size verification, then ran both baseline and repaired hooks with PIP_NO_INDEX=1 and PIP_FIND_LINKS=wheelhouse, fresh PRE_COMMIT_HOME, PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1, restricted PATH, and an explicit pre-check that the launcher had neither jsonschema nor referencing. The baseline reproduced exit 1 with 'GEC_VALIDATION_UNAVAILABLE: ModuleNotFoundError' (47 tests, 16 failures, 5 errors); the repaired hook passed 47 tests with exit 0, and the hook venv (prefix != base_prefix) contained jsonschema 4.26.0 and referencing 0.37.0. This is a faithful clean-environment repro, but resolution behaviour against a live index (what CI will do) was not exercised.

nonblocking_risks.title: Dependency is an unpinned floor (`jsonschema>=4.20.0`) resolved from PyPI at hook-install time
nonblocking_risks.detail: `referencing` is obtained only transitively (jsonschema 4.26.0 declares `referencing>=0.28.4`); the hook env is therefore resolved at install time in CI without version or hash pinning, so it is not byte-reproducible over time and depends on jsonschema continuing to declare referencing. This matches the existing repository pattern (the proof-embedded-audit-schema hook uses unpinned `jsonschema`; pyproject declares `jsonschema>=4.20.0`), and jsonschema has required referencing since 4.18, so the practical risk is low. A stricter follow-up could pin jsonschema (and optionally list referencing explicitly) in a separate packet.

nonblocking_risks.title: Parent validation logs are bare outputs without captured commands, exit codes, or environment preconditions
nonblocking_risks.detail: PARENT_ISOLATED_HOOK.log shows a fresh 'local:jsonschema>=4.20.0' environment being initialized and 47 tests OK, PARENT_CT_TESTS.log shows 47 OK, PARENT_GEC_TESTS.log shows 590 passed, PARENT_CHANGED_PRECOMMIT.log shows all hooks Passed/Skipped, and PARENT_DIFF_CHECK.log is empty (sha256 of empty input, consistent with a clean `git diff --check` but the exit code is only asserted by the receipt). The receipt (writer_custody 'shell/local', model_calls 0) binds each log by sha256 matching FILE_INVENTORY, but does not show that the parent isolated run's launcher lacked jsonschema (only the Codex run has that explicit check), and the parent re-run occurred on the same machine ~5 minutes after the implementer's run, so environmental independence is limited.

nonblocking_risks.title: The CT hook's `files:` filter excludes `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, so the changed-file pre-commit for H1 itself skipped the hook
nonblocking_risks.detail: Both the implementer's and the parent's changed-file pre-commit runs report 'Validate Control Tower kit contracts ... (no files to check) Skipped'. Hook correctness therefore rests on the separate isolated hook runs, which is acceptable. On PR 1360 the hook will execute because the M0 branch touches `.control-tower/` and `schemas/governed_execution/`, but future edits to the hook stanza alone will not self-test.
